chase_cards.name: No.1 Trainer [World Challenge Tropical Mega Battle regional first place]
chase_cards.why: This is a chase because it is not merely a card that says No.1. It is a personalized credential from the Japanese regional route toward Tropical Mega Battle and the World Exchange Battle in Hawaii: a paper trophy for a player who actually won their way into the world-stage machinery.

key_artists.name: Ken Sugimori
examples: No.1 Trainer [World Challenge Tropical Mega Battle regional first place]
key_artists.why: Sugimori matters here because this trophy card borrows authority from the person who made early Pokémon visually legible in the first place. The card is competitive infrastructure, but the image language comes from the franchise's central visual architect.

claims.text: The local catalog models the World Challenge Tropical Mega Battle regional first-place source group as one row containing No.1 Trainer at source index 174.
Bulbapedia says No.1 Trainer began as a Japanese tournament Trainer card and later became a first-place prize in the Pokémon World Championships.

Bulbapedia says the World Challenge Summer 2000 No.1 Trainer iteration was first awarded to champions of each regional Japanese World Challenge Summer event held between July and August 2000, with the circuit split into Tropical Mega Battle and Secret Super Battle events.

Bulbapedia says overall winners of the Tropical Mega Battle regional events represented their country in the World Exchange Battle in Hawaii, while remaining top-ranking players competed in a domestic Best in Japan final, both held in late August 2000.

Bulbapedia lists the World Challenge Summer 2000 regional conferences for No.1 Trainer as Kantō, Kansai, Hokkaidō, Chūbu, Hokushin'etsu, Kyūshū, Chūgoku/Shikoku, and Tōhoku, with events from July 1 through August 6, 2000.
Bulbapedia says the World Challenge Summer 2000 No.1 Trainer cards were personalized with the winner's name and regional conference and were Non Holofoil.

Bulbapedia says two base versions exist for the World Challenge Summer 2000 No.1 Trainer, one depicting a male Trainer and one depicting a female Trainer, with the awarded version depending on the winner's gender.
Bulbapedia says the World Challenge Summer No.1 Trainer major iteration used new artwork by Ken Sugimori.

Bulbapedia describes Ken Sugimori as a friend of Satoshi Tajiri, illustrator of the original Pokémon game artwork, illustrator of TCG cards and merchandise, and the artist who redrew all 151 Generation I Pokémon in watercolor for promotional use.

Bulbapedia describes Tropical Mega Battle as an international TCG tournament held annually from 1999 through 2001 at Hilton Hawaiian Village in Honolulu, involving top players from Canada, Latin America, Europe, the United States, and Japan, with about 50 players each year.

Bulbapedia warns that Tropical Mega Battle No.1 Trainer prints are often misconceived as overall finals prizes, while they were awarded to qualifying event winners; this dossier applies that warning to keep regional first-place prize identity separate from Best in Japan and finals labels.

Pokumon identifies Girl TMB No.1 Trainer (World Challenge Summer 2000) as the World Challenge Tropical Mega Battle 2000 regional first-place prize, tags it as a Japanese unnumbered non-holo Trainer Winner card illustrated by Ken Sugimori, and presents an estimated copy count for that gendered version; this dossier treats the count as collector estimate, not official disclosure.

Heritage describes a No.1 Trainer Tropical Mega Battle card as a regional first-place prize that qualified winners for the international Tropical Mega Battle and notes that the card was never sold commercially, framing it as a tournament-awarded trophy rather than a retail chase.

As judged collector texture, this regional No.1 Trainer matters because it is a signed social position in cardboard form: winner name, region, gendered base art, tournament route, and possible Hawaii path all appear before any modern price conversation begins.

narrative.human_title: No.1 Trainer [World Challenge Tropical Mega Battle regional]: a name, a region, a door to Hawaii
narrative.why_it_matters: This is the kind of trophy card where the object is almost less interesting than what the object proves happened around it. A player won a regional World Challenge Summer route, their name and conference were carried onto the card, and the Tropical Mega Battle path pointed toward Hawaii and an early international stage before Worlds had fully hardened into the structure collectors know now. Sugimori's artwork gives it franchise gravity, but the real charge is assembly: child player, region, tournament bracket, printed honor, and a possible world-stage invitation all locked into one unnumbered promo.
not_claiming: that every No.1 Trainer listing uses this same route

special_identification_instructions.trigger: Use when a card, listing, slab label, auction description, or agent claim says No.1 Trainer, World Challenge, Tropical Mega Battle, regional first place, TMB, Hawaii qualifier, male Trainer, female Trainer, personalized name, or Best in Japan.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Treat No.1 Trainer as a reusable trophy-card title. Establish the exact route before comparing value, rarity, or historical meaning.
steps: Confirm the card is No.1 Trainer / Ｎｏ.１トレーナー and that the claimed promotion is World Challenge Tropical Mega Battle regional first-place prize, not Secret Super Battle, Best in Japan, 1999 Tropical Mega Battle, Lizardon Mega Battle, Kamex Mega Battle, Neo Road, Battle Road, or World Championships.

Check whether the card is the 2000 World Challenge Summer regional version: non-holo, personalized with winner name and regional conference, and based on male or female Trainer artwork depending on winner gender.

Verify the route language: regional Tropical Mega Battle first-place winners fed toward the Hawaii / World Exchange Battle path, while remaining top-ranking players fed into the domestic Best in Japan final. Do not collapse those into one prize class.

Use the regional conference/date list as a plausibility rail: Kantō, Kansai, Hokkaidō, Chūbu, Hokushin'etsu, Kyūshū, Chūgoku/Shikoku, and Tōhoku were the World Challenge Summer regional stops from July 1 through August 6, 2000.
Record collector-estimated copy counts only as estimates. Do not convert Pokumon or auction copy language into an official print run.

Before spending or trade gating, require seller-controlled photos of the actual card, including name/conference personalization, front/back, surface, edge, and any slab label; catalog identity is legible support, not physical truth.
not_claiming: that No.1 Trainer name alone identifies the exact print
that a grading label alone resolves the route

context.name_en: No.1 Trainer [World Challenge Tropical Mega Battle regional first place]

claims.text: The local catalog row identifies source index 174 as No.1 Trainer from the World Challenge Tropical Mega Battle regional first-place prize slice.
Bulbapedia gives the Japanese name as Ｎｏ.１トレーナー and describes No.1 Trainer as a Japanese tournament Trainer/Item card lineage used for first-place prizes.

Bulbapedia says the World Challenge Summer 2000 No.1 Trainer regional cards were personalized with the winner's name and regional conference, non-holo, and split into male and female Trainer base versions.
Bulbapedia identifies Ken Sugimori as the artist for the World Challenge Summer No.1 Trainer major iteration.

As interpretive art context, Sugimori's credit gives the card a direct line back to the visual standardization of Pokémon: the same hand associated with original game artwork and the watercolor public image of the first 151 is now authorizing a tournament winner's object.

This card must be separated from World Challenge Tropical Mega Battle Best in Japan No.1 Trainer, World Challenge Secret Super Battle No.1 Trainer, 1999 Tropical Mega Battle No.1 Trainer, Lizardon Mega Battle, Kamex Mega Battle, Neo Road, Battle Road, and World Championships No.1 Trainer prints.

As judged collector texture, No.1 Trainer [World Challenge Tropical Mega Battle regional first place] is interesting because it is a named winner's credential first and a collectible second: the personalization, region, and route are the card's reason to exist.

narrative.human_title: No.1 Trainer: the card as a tournament credential
narrative.why_it_matters: This is not a normal chase card wearing a trophy-card costume. Its identity is procedural: win the regional route, get your name and conference printed into the object, and stand at the fork between domestic Best in Japan and the international Tropical Mega Battle machinery. That makes it wonderful for this catalog because the card forces an agent to care about assembly: event, age division, route, gendered artwork, personalization, and artist credit all matter before the card can even be named cleanly.
not_claiming: that every No.1 Trainer print follows this route

special_identification_instructions.trigger: Use when evaluating a specific No.1 Trainer image, listing, slab, or seller claim connected to World Challenge Tropical Mega Battle regional first place.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Identify this card by exact trophy route and personalization, not by the reusable No.1 Trainer title.
steps: Confirm the card title is No.1 Trainer / Ｎｏ.１トレーナー and the route is World Challenge Tropical Mega Battle regional first-place prize.
Check for 2000 regional personalization: winner name and regional conference should be part of the identity claim, and the card should be non-holo for this regional class.
Determine whether the image is the male Trainer or female Trainer base version; do not treat gendered art as a defect or unrelated variant without route context.

Separate regional first-place cards from World Challenge Tropical Mega Battle Best in Japan cards, which are a different prize class, and from Secret Super Battle cards, which follow the parallel event track.
Separate this print from 1999 Tropical Mega Battle, Lizardon Mega Battle, Kamex Mega Battle, Neo Spring/Summer Road, Battle Road, and World Championships No.1 Trainer prints.

Before spending or trade gating, require seller-controlled photos of the actual card, including personalization, front/back, surface, edge, and slab label if graded; catalog identity is legible support, not physical truth.
not_claiming: that a grading label alone resolves the route
that catalog identity makes the evidence spendable
